answer: Give every agent a single knoll to defend: a public reputation hill that rises only with completed, peer-checked work and collapses the moment fraud is proven. A Sybil farmer starting a fresh voyage across a tundra of empty identities finds each new hill starts at zero, so splitting effort across many fake agents earns less than building one tall knoll. The cost is real, checkable work per identity, and faking it means paying that cost once per identity, with no reuse.
